headline: Money Leaves Chips for Consumer and Housing Names as Most Stocks Rise
body_html:
Thursday's session ended with a clear majority of stocks higher: 377 of the 536 names we track rose and 156 fell. The index-level picture mattered less than where the money went. Capital moved out of semiconductors and into consumer, housing and industrial shares.

Consumer led the sector table with a gain of 2.59%, just ahead of homebuilders at 2.56%. Industrials added 1.87% and healthcare 1.57%, while materials rose 0.92% and software 0.88%. Energy slipped 0.44%, and semiconductors were the weakest group, down 1.28%. Marvell Technology fell 13.24% and FormFactor 11.65%. Fortinet dropped 20.09%, a reminder that a rising software group still had sharp losers inside it.

The standout mover was Glaukos, up 33.65%, with Crocs close behind at 25.54% and Boot Barn up 15.16%. Builders FirstSource gained 12.85% and Flowserve 11.89%. On the downside, Alnylam fell 25.13%, the steepest drop among the names we track. The message was selective rather than defensive: investors trimmed chip exposure but kept buying elsewhere. Friday's session will show whether that rotation has staying power.

briefs.headline: Alphabet Draws Harsher Treatment Than Microsoft
briefs.body: Market commentary on Thursday focused on why investors are punishing Alphabet after its latest quarter while giving Microsoft a pass. At least one analyst downgraded the stock and laid out the price levels at which it would turn buyer again.

briefs.headline: Insurer Flags Financing Risk in AI Data Centers
briefs.body: The chief executive of Aon warned that insurance risks tied to AI data centers could threaten how those projects get financed. The comment adds a cautionary note to the heavy building cycle behind the sector, and it landed on a day when chip stocks lagged.

briefs.headline: Crypto-Linked Shares Jump on a Rare Druckenmiller Post
briefs.body: A crypto-linked stock surged after Stanley Druckenmiller, who rarely posts publicly, weighed in on social media. The move showed how quickly sentiment in the corner of the market can shift on a single comment from a well-known investor.

briefs.headline: Polymarket Halts Trading After International Outage
briefs.body: Polymarket reported an outage on its international exchange and halted trading there. The platform gave no immediate timetable for a return, and the episode highlights the operational fragility of newer trading venues.

briefs.headline: European Earnings Season Tracking Near Post-2022 Highs
briefs.body: Corporate Europe is heading for its second-strongest earnings season since 2022, according to Reuters. The report offers a firmer backdrop for overseas equities even as U.S. investors sorted through a lopsided sector rotation at home.

briefs.headline: Qatar Buys LNG Cargoes to Hedge Against Hormuz Risk
briefs.body: QatarEnergy is buying liquefied natural gas from the U.S. and other suppliers to cover possible future disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reported. Energy shares slipped 0.44% on the session as traders weighed the geopolitical backdrop.
